links.targetTitle: Interim Deployments let a Prime allocate real capital before

title: New assets are onboarded through ratcheted deployment tranches with per-tranche human approval, not through a single limit
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.3 governs Superstate deployments in two steps rather than one cap. The Initial Deployment — "the first deployment of capital by a Prime Agent into Superstate Exposures" — "may not exceed 20,000,000 USDS." Each Subsequent Deployment "may not exceed 50,000,000 USDS and requires approval from the Core Council Risk Advisor on behalf of the Core Council."

The same pattern appears in A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.3.1.1 for JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche, with more layers: a 20m USDS combined initial deployment, Risk Advisor approval for "each additional deployment," a 250m total ceiling, and a pre-condition tied to an unfinished audit — "until audits of Centrifuge v3 are approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, the Prime must be below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio on a pro forma basis assuming that each additional deployment ... requires 100% Instance Total CRR."

The pattern is a *staged commitment* rather than a limit. A single ceiling permits the whole exposure on day one, so all the information Sky would gain from watching the position perform arrives after the risk is already taken. Small first tranche plus approval-gated increments converts the ceiling into a sequence of decisions, each made with more evidence than the last, and each cheap to stop.

The Centrifuge condition is the most interesting variant because it is a *counterfactual* test. The Agent is not required to hold 100% capital against the new deployment; it is required to remain below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio in a world where it did. That reserves headroom for the possibility that the audit comes back badly and the exposure is reclassified — the Agent must be able to survive the downgrade before it is allowed to take the position.

A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.3.1.2 shows the same machinery running in reverse for an asset being wound down: ACRDX exposure "may not increase beyond 50.97 million USDS and should be reduced to zero over time" — a frozen, decaying allowance rather than an immediate forced exit.
description: Superstate allows a 20m USDS first deployment then 50m increments each needing Risk Advisor approval; Avalanche JTRSY/JAAA adds a 250m ceiling and an audit-contingent Encumbrance test.
